newsitem.title: USA: NJ Gov expected to sign $4.9 bln school bill - paper.
newsitem.headline: NJ Gov expected to sign $4.9 bln school bill - paper.

text.p: New Jersey Governor Christie Whitman is expected Friday to sign a school funding bill passed Thursday by the state legislature that to strives to meet the Supreme Court's demand to put rich and poor districts on an even keel, The Record reported Friday.

The legislature's approval of the $4.9 billion measure capped more than a year of debate, the newspaper said. The Record quoted Whitman as predicting that the measure would lead to "vast improvement over what is taught in New Jersey's schools."
Poor districts who contend the bill will actually broaden the spending gap between poor city schools and wealthier suburban districts, are expected to mount a legal challenge.

Whitman, who thinks the bill can withstand a court challenge, acknowledged that while it fails to answer the Supreme Court's order to equalize spending, new academic standards for all districts would meet the high court's call for equity, the Record reported.
